items: A bare `*args, **kwargs` erases the signature for type checkers
Choose `@` when a concern is cross-cutting and repeated
No `@wraps`: docs, logs and pytest ids all read `wrapper`
No `return` inside the wrapper: every call yields None
No `return wrapper`: the decorated name itself becomes None
`@deco` vs `@deco()` mixup: `TypeError: deco() missing 1 required positional argument`
Loop closures see the final loop value — bind with a default arg
Mutable state in factory scope is shared by every decorated function
One stateful instance reused across functions bleeds state between them

blocks.title: Method Cache Leak
blocks.text: `@lru_cache` on a method keys on `self` and pins that instance forever. Use `cached_property` or a per-instance cache.

caption.text: Part 2 of PYTHON HANDBOOK. Every Python decorator you have ever written is one line of sugar over `f = deco(f)` — and every weird bug in one traces back to a closure cell you never looked inside. This handbook goes from first-class functions and LEGB scope through wraps, argument forwarding, factories, class-based decorators and stacking order, then lands on the patterns you actually ship: cache, retry, timing, auth, registration. Ten pages, one save, the whole wrapping model.
